name: Meaningful source and focus order through responsive relocation
summary: When visual regions move across viewport conditions, programmatic reading and keyboard focus sequences remain meaningful and operable where sequence matters.
problem: A CSS rearrangement may visually reprioritize panels while preserving a focus route that no longer makes sense for the task.
context: Responsive changes to visual order of controls, navigation, content or pane regions.
observed_solution: Review source reading sequence, visual order and sequential keyboard path as distinct concerns; revise structure or interaction design if meaning/operability is disrupted.
rationale: WCAG 1.3.1 relationships (O01), 1.3.2 conditional meaningful sequence (O02) and 2.4.3 focus order (O07) are normative within their scope; Primer pinned PageLayout region-order/position code shows possible layout-level reordering (O29/O30/O32).
tradeoffs: Visual and source order need not be identical for independent regions.
Making separate DOM copies can introduce focus/semantics risks, untested here.
applicability: Meaning-bearing content order or sequentially keyboard-navigated interactions changed in a narrow viewport.
non_applicability: Purely decorative reordering with no reading or focus meaning effect.
Nonsequential spatial exploration where WCAG conditions do not apply in the same way.
accessibility_implications: Actual target must be checked against SC 1.3.1, 1.3.2 and 2.4.3; no automatic violation from CSS order alone.
responsive_implications: Test order transitions at relevant layout changes, not named device models.
implementation_notes: Use standard- and context-based validation; do not prescribe React or a DOM-reordering algorithm.
Pinned code is a mechanics example only.

counterexamples.summary: Repositioning unrelated decorative panels may not affect reading meaning or focus operability.
